newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dollar drags Euro stocks lower amid lira row.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dollar drags Euro stocks lower amid lira row.

text.p: The dollar fell after a strong start on Tuesday, the indirect victim of a fresh row over Italy's fitness to join the single European currency.
The dollar also propelled continental European stock markets to record levels early in the day, and promptly pulled them back down when it dropped through the 1.70 mark level.
But dealers said that the dollar's modest losses were unlikely to last long as the fundamental point remained: the U.S. economy is strong and the German economy weak.
"It's been a corrective day, but nothing's changed. Germany's still in trouble and America's still looking good," said a dealer at a Swiss bank in London.

At one point, the dollar hit a 34-month record of 1.7050 marks. But it could not hold at such heights and slipped to 1.6875 marks by the European close, well below 1.6997 at the same time on Monday. It also slipped to 123.85 yen from 124.50 on Monday.

Dealers attributed the early strength to fears about the health of China's paramount leader, 92-year-old Deng Xiaoping. A skirmish between Iranian forces and members of an opposition group based in Iraq also provoked dollar buying.
But the mood swiftly changed as uncertainty over European economic and monetary union (EMU) surfaced again.
The primary victim was the lira, which tumbled amid concern that Italy might not make the first wave of EMU. The lira fell to 996.65 to the mark from 987.25 late on Monday.

Dealers blamed comments from Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Belgian central bank chief Alfonse Verplaetse. Prodi said on Monday that Germany was less committed to EMU than Italy, fuelling rumours that Bonn was conspiring to keep the lira out of the first wave of nations joining the European currency's launch.
Verplaetse also made comments apparently questioning the lira's ability to join EMU early, although he later denied he had been referring to Italy.
"This is building up into a bit of a row between Italy and Germany and all the underlying tensions are gradually coming to the surface," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy.

The mark's strength against the lira had a knock-on effect which also strengthened it against the dollar. "The lira's fallen out of bed and the mark's benefiting from that..but nothing fundamentally has changed in perceptions of the dollar," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB in London.

The peseta also fell amid reports of Bank of Spain intervention as sentiment hit the southern European currencies. Sterling was also a major casualty, plunging to 2.7053 marks from 2.7445 late on Monday after an apparent softening of the Bank of England's hawkish inflation stance.
Governor Eddie George said on Monday that a spate of British economic data, along with sterling's strength, had made the need for an interest rate rise less urgent than was thought in December.
The dollar pulled continental European stocks up in the morning to record levels and then dragged them back down.

Germany's DAX index, which closes early, ended up 43.59 points, or 1.35 percent, at a record 3,276.16. But in after-hours electronic trading a feeling that the market needed to consolidate after this year's bull run gained strength and the IBIS index closed down 29.47 points at 3,230.83.
France's CAC-40 index likewise fell after a powerful start, and closed down 16.96 points at 2,617.52. "It's logical to take profits at these levels," one Paris dealer said.
London had awaited Wall Street for guidance after the long holdiday weekend in the United States, but found little.
By the European close, the Dow Jones Industrial average was down 5.78 points at 6,983.18 after a choppy morning.
London's FTSE 100 index closed down 5.5 points at 4,332.3 after an uninspiring session.
Dealers blamed Wall Street plus disappointing results from Barclays Plc. The bank posted pre-tax profits of 2.36 billion pounds ($3.8 billion), at the low end of expectations.

However, one uncertainty disappeared, for the time being at least, when the Conservative government survived a parliamentary censure motion on Monday night which could have led to a confidence vote and an early election.
CURRENCIES AT EUROPEAN CLOSE
The dollar was quoted at 1.6875 marks and 123.85 yen compared with 1.6997 marks and 124.50 yen in late European trading on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 5.5 points at 4,332.3
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed down 16.96 at 2,617.52 points.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed 43.59 points higher at a record 3,276.16.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $345.60 an ounce after an afternoon fixing at $345.00 an ounce and Monday's closing at $344.25. Silver closed three cents firmer at $5.24.
